artists.biography: The Bangles are an American all-female band that originated in the early 1980s, scoring several hit singles during the decade. Susanna Hoffs joined sisters Vicki and Debbi Peterson to form a band in Los Angeles in December, 1980. The trio briefly called themselves The Colours, then renamed themselves The Supersonic Bangs, and shortly afterwards The Bangs. The band was part of the Los Angeles Paisley Underground scene, which featured groups that played a mixture of 1960s-influenced folk-rock and jangle pop with a more modern punk-ish/garage band undertone. In 1981, the threesome recorded and released a single ("Getting Out Of Hand" b/w "Call on Me") on DownKiddie Records (their own label). The trio was signed to Faulty Products, a label formed by Miles Copeland. In 1982, Susanna Hoffs asked long time friend, Patrick Hirtz, to manage the band until his departure in 1986 to pursue the culinary arts. The early Bangles line-up of Susanna Hoffs (vocals/guitars), Vicki Peterson (guitars/vocals), Debbi Peterson (vocals/drums) and Annette Zilinskas (vocals/bass) recorded an EP in 1982, and released the single "The Real World". A legal issue forced the band to change their name at the last minute so they dropped "The" and added the letters "les" to the end to become Bangles. Their first EP was retitled Bangles and released. In 1983, Faulty Products issued a 12 inch "remix" single of "The Real World" to radio and media, but another setback came as the label folded. I.R.S. Records picked up distribution and re-issued the EP. After Zilinskas left the band to focus on her own project Blood on the Saddle, she was replaced by Michael Steele, formerly of the all-girl band The Runaways, Toni & The Movers, Slow Children and Elton Duck.

perplexity.description:
Different Light is the Bangles' second studio album, released in January 1986 by Columbia Records. Marking a stylistic shift from their earlier 1960s-inspired rock sound, the album embraces a polished pop rock and mainstream Top 40 aesthetic. It is notable for featuring bassist Michael Steele singing lead vocals on some tracks for the first time in the band's discography.

The album includes several successful singles, most prominently "Manic Monday," written by Prince, and the No. 1 hit "Walk Like an Egyptian." These singles, along with others like "If She Knew What She Wants" and "Walking Down Your Street," helped Different Light become the Bangles' best-known and most commercially successful release. The album's accessible sound and catchy songwriting secured strong chart performances and established the band firmly in the mid-1980s pop rock scene.
